title: u rgyan padma'i rnam thar/ rin po che 'od 'bar ba (in Tibetan Headless letter)
shelf_note: A dbu med manuscript of a Padmasambhava biography (chapter 2 colophon on p.5: ཨྱོན་པདྨའི་རྣམ་ཐར་ལས་ ... ལེའུ་སྟེ་གཉིས་པའོ; a chapter on prophesied treasure-revealers on p.188) from the Ogyen Choling collection. It belongs on a Bhutanese/Tibetan Nyingma shelf.
structure_note: Every image is a board with three loose leaves (I5). The site's pages interleave: p.5's leaf 1 ends 'འདོམ་ཅན་གྱི་མཚོ་' and continues on p.6's leaf 1 'ཁར་ཕྱིན་པར་གྱུར་'. p.6 leaf 1 continues on p.5 leaf 2, and p.5 leaf 3 continues on p.6 leaf 3. So p.6 holds the versos of p.5's rectos, and no single page reads straight through. The OCR carries <leaf-break/> markers and the translation keeps the leaves apart. Only 8 of 236 pages are translated; all 236 have OCR. 104 repeats among 107 printed numbers fit three leaves per frame with marginal numerals that repeat; I read it as the board structure, not a splice. The images are only 1536 px wide for three leaves of headless script, which is too small for word-level checking.

ocr_errors.image: cannot resolve at this resolution; p.6's praise names the lake འོ་མ་ཅན་གྱི་རྒྱ་མཚོ (milk lake)
ocr_errors.problem: lake name probably misread (milk lake → 'dom can')

tr_errors.english: ...is the supreme teacher of the excellent Goodness.
tr_errors.problem: Bzang po mchog is the king's name (p.6 translates it 'King Zangpo Chok'). The clause says he was made the king's chaplain (bla mchod); the English turns it into an abstraction.

tr_errors.english: the realm of Great Bliss <note>original: "Sukhavati"</note>
tr_errors.problem: The note says the original reads 'Sukhavati'; the OCR reads bde ba chen po, not bde ba can

tr_errors.english: Five youths questioned Amitabha
tr_errors.problem: On p.6 the youths tell the king to ask Amitabha, and the speech here asks about 'these five youths', so the king is likely the questioner. Doubtful agent.

tr_errors.english: the one called "Mighty Sage of Stainless Nose"
tr_errors.problem: A proper name rendered literally. 'sna' is probably a misread (e.g. zla, moon), and the result is absurd.

ocr_errors.problem: Probably མཛོ་མོ་ཁྱུ་གཅིག་འཚོ (herding dzo cattle). The OCR gives 'leper women' and 'lake', and the translation follows it.

tr_errors.english: "Famine Tresses", "The condensed Bön of famine", "famine priests <note>original: "mu ge bla mchod"</note>"
tr_errors.problem: mu ge is a name or party in the Bön/heretic debate, probably mu stegs (tirthika). Rendered as 'famine' throughout, it gives a reader nonsense ('famine priests' summoned to the king) and hides that these are the heretic priests.

tr_errors.english: If that daughter and the one with one head and the fish Keshi tamed them together
tr_errors.problem: 'the one born to that girl' (her son) becomes 'the one with one head'

tr_errors.english: While she sat there among a group of lepers by a lake
tr_errors.problem: Built on the garbled OCR: she was herding a herd, not sitting among lepers by a lake

tr_errors.english: If a single wall <note>uncertain: "gyang"</note> comes, because there is no actual support for the ghost
tr_errors.problem: Garbled clause rendered as confident nonsense, with only a weak hedge

book_verdict: These are the right leaves, transcribed as separate leaves with seam markers, but each site page is a recto/verso jumble of three leaves. The images are too small to check the headless script word by word. The English is fluent and mostly holds, but p.104 turns the 'mu ge' heretics into 'famine' throughout.
reader_summary: A headless-script manuscript of a Padmasambhava biography (Amitābha's emanations, the lotus-born youths and King Zangpo Chok, later prophecies of treasure-revealers). The transcription is of the right leaves, but each page shows three leaves, and only 8 of 236 pages have English. The English follows the narrative but misreads proper names, and on p.104 it renders a recurring name as 'famine'. Treat names and rare terms as unchecked.

title: Phurdrup Gonpa Thor bu bKa' thang sde lnga
shelf_note: A dbu can manuscript of the bKa' thang sde lnga (the Five Chronicles revealed by O rgyan gling pa): the princess's hell-journey chapter (ch.11), the rivers of empowerment and the founding of Samye (ch.10), the Vimalakirti non-duality list and translation history (ch.14 of the lha 'dre/lha chos section), and prophecies. It is a core Nyingma treasure text.
structure_note: Every image is a board with three leaves (I5), each opening with ༄༅། on the rectos; the OCR marks <leaf-break/> between them. The leaves on one page are not consecutive (p.13: leaf 1 ends on the road to Nepal, leaf 2 is the hell scene, leaf 3 closes ch.11). 232 of 257 pages are translated. The one printed number means no backstep data. Chapter numbering restarts (ch.11 on p.13, ch.10 on p.68, ch.14 on p.166), which is expected for five books bound as one.

ocr_errors.image: a row of gter cipher marks after the ch.11 colophon
ocr_errors.problem: Latin 'KK' emitted in Tibetan text for the cipher glyphs

tr_errors.english: Since there is no compassion for a hundred men
tr_errors.problem: The source means 'you hundred men have no compassion'; the English reverses who lacks compassion

tr_errors.english: the mother Shakyadevi
tr_errors.problem: The mother's name (Shakya Trima) is replaced by Shakyadevi, the name already used for the Nepalese consort, so two people merge

tr_errors.english: The decline of such a girl is the way of the path; let her cast aside the directions.
tr_errors.problem: Fluent nonsense for a prayer that the girl's misery be removed

other.note: <meta>continues from previous page</meta> opens the English

tr_errors.english: Jnanakumara, and Kharchen Tsogyal
tr_errors.problem: The source has Kumaraja; the translator substitutes the expected figure

ocr_errors.image: cipher marks after the ch.14 colophon
ocr_errors.problem: Latin letters for Tibetan cipher glyphs

tr_errors.english: The *Proceeding on the Path* was translated in fifteen volumes.
tr_errors.problem: This is the Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra (Lang kar gshegs pa); in a list of translated scriptures the English invents a non-existent title

tr_errors.english: if sentient beings are free from the stains of the Dharma
tr_errors.problem: Inverted: the Dharma is free of the stains of beings, not beings free of the Dharma's stains

tr_errors.english: there is no reason to be clever. Be patient, do not be clever
tr_errors.problem: 'mkhang' (probably mkhon, resentment) rendered as 'clever'; the teaching is 'bear it without resentment'

tr_errors.english: will be led away in the manner of priests and offerings
tr_errors.problem: bla mchod is 'court chaplain' (taken away as chaplains), not 'priests and offerings'

tr_errors.english: Red spears and Chinese swords; the five-continent copper-men
tr_errors.problem: Garbled prophecy line rendered as fluent fragments with no uncertainty marker

other.note: <meta>continues from previous page: describing future disturbances and the locations for refuge.</meta>, a translator's summary at the head of the page

book_verdict: The dbu can script is transcribed very well, and the leaves are right and marked. The English reads smoothly but carries real slips: an invented sutra title for the Laṅkāvatāra, an inverted doctrinal clause, and two people merged under one name.
reader_summary: The bKa' thang sde lnga, O rgyan gling pa's five treasure chronicles (the queens, the ministers, the gods and demons, the translators), in a clear headed-script manuscript. The transcription is of the right text and very close to the page. The English is usable for the narrative, but names, titles and doctrinal clauses need checking against the Tibetan. Each page holds three separate leaves, not a continuous passage.

title: O rgyan pad ma 'byung gnas kyi skyes rabs rnam thar
shelf_note: A dbu med illuminated manuscript (lotus painting on p.22) of a Padmasambhava life-story (skyes rabs rnam thar): Indrabhūti's wish-fulfilling jewel (ch.14–15), Garab Dorje and Mañjuśrīmitra, the charnel grounds, and the farewell testaments (ch.117–118). Gangtey Monastery collection; it fits.
structure_note: Each image is a board with four leaves (I5); the OCR has four <leaf-break/> segments per page, which matches. Rubrics and colophons fall where the image shows red ink (p.22 leaf 4 'བཅོ་ལྔ་པའོ', p.161 leaves 1–2 ch.117/118). Only 45 of 166 pages are translated, and pages_ocr (54) disagrees with the 166 pages that carry OCR. The one backstep among 3 printed numbers is negligible.

ocr_errors.image: no letter O on the leaf
ocr_errors.problem: stray full-width Latin 'Ｏ' in the transcription

tr_errors.english: Seeing the boy bobbing along as a prize
tr_errors.problem: The subject is the hooked fish dangling, not the boy; it blurs the image the boy then reflects on

tr_errors.english: The mother recognized this as the sign of a "comfortable corpse" <note>a spiritual realization</note>
tr_errors.problem: Literal rendering plus an explanatory note that asserts a meaning the source does not give

tr_errors.english: He became an emanation of a white-fleshed fish.
tr_errors.problem: Probably a fish named Kesha (cf. ཀེ་ཤ elsewhere in the story) read as 'white flesh'

tr_errors.english: Because they are attached to the Dharma <note>the text implies a superficial or corrupt attachment</note>, they are of the race of the black Mara.
tr_errors.problem: In a list of vices the clause must be hostile to the Dharma. The English makes it 'attached' and adds a note to explain away the contradiction.

tr_errors.english: even if you treat them quickly, it is like turning an ocean into a meadow
tr_errors.problem: Garbled source rendered as a confident simile

other.note: the English opens its last leaf with a model note: '<note>This leaf appears to record the lamentation of the Tibetan people as the Guru prepares to leave.</note>'

book_verdict: The transcription of the headless script is close to the leaves, and the English is careful and readable on all four pages. Only small slips and one explained-away inversion on p.161.
reader_summary: An illustrated headless-script life of Padmasambhava, from Indrabhūti's jewel and the lake-born child through Garab Dorje and the charnel grounds to his last testaments to doctors and the Tibetan people. The transcription is of the right leaves, and the English can largely be trusted for the story. Each page holds four separate leaves, and three-quarters of the book has no English yet.

title: Pad 'byung rnam thar
shelf_note: A dbu can manuscript of a Padmasambhava biography of the Zangs gling ma type: subduing the gods and demons for Samye, Vimalamitra's birth and the invitation, and the farewell testaments to geshes (ch.27), mantrins and women (ch.32). Gangtey Monastery collection; it fits.
structure_note: Each image is a board with three leaves (I5): rectos with ༄༅༅ on p.25/51/81, versos without on p.86. <leaf-break/> markers are present. 95 of 106 pages are translated; nothing else stands out.

ocr_errors.problem: ན་བཟའ (robe) split and misread, though the translation still gives 'robes'

tr_errors.english: On a bowl full of onyx-bead-like tormas
tr_errors.problem: a zi-stone bowl filled with torma, not tormas like onyx beads

other.note: each leaf's English ends in '<note>the text cuts off at the leaf end</note>', apparatus a reader sees three times on one page

tr_errors.english: The boat depends upon a single point
tr_errors.problem: doubtful rendering of a riddle term; small

tr_errors.english: you will become a mimic among women
tr_errors.problem: loose rendering of a proverb

book_verdict: A clean headed-script manuscript with an accurate transcription and a faithful, plain English. Only minor slips on four pages.
reader_summary: A life of Padmasambhava in the Zangs gling ma tradition: the taming of the spirits for Samye, the invitation of Vimalamitra, and the Guru's parting advice to scholars, tantrikas and the women of Tibet. The transcription matches the leaves closely, and the English follows it faithfully. Each page holds three leaves, read leaf by leaf.
